title: Lamb Chops with Salsa Verde
subtitle: Pan-fried lamb chops with a herby Italian green sauce
excerpt: Salsa verde is one of the most versatile sauces in the Italian kitchen. Made from parsley, mint, capers, anchovies and good olive oil, it cuts through the richness of pan-fried lamb chops perfectly. The sauce takes five minutes to make while the lamb rests.
sourceNotes: Salsa verde is a classic condiment from northern Italy, particularly Lombardy and Piedmont, where it traditionally accompanies bollito misto. Pairing it with grilled or pan-fried lamb has become widespread across Italian cooking.

recipe.makeAheadNotes: Salsa verde can be made up to 2 hours ahead and kept covered at room temperature.

content.text: Chop the herbs by hand rather than blending for a sauce with more texture. A roughly chopped salsa verde has more character than a smooth puree.

items.prepNote: cut into chops or ask your butcher

content.text: Make the salsa verde. Finely chop the parsley, mint, capers, garlic and anchovies together on a board until you have a rough paste. Scrape into a bowl.
Stir in the olive oil, red wine vinegar and Dijon mustard. Season with salt and pepper. Set aside.
Season the lamb chops generously on both sides with salt and pepper.

Heat a large frying pan over a high heat until very hot. Add the chops in a single layer (work in batches) and cook for 3 minutes per side for medium, or 2 minutes per side for pink. Do not move them between turns.
Rest the chops on a warm plate for 5 minutes, then serve with the salsa verde spooned over.

items.symptom: Lamb is grey and steamed rather than seared.
items.cause: Too many chops were in the pan at once.
items.fix: Cook in batches so chops have space and the pan stays hot.

items.cause: Anchovies and capers added without adjusting other seasoning.
items.fix: Taste before adding any extra salt. The anchovies season it.
